name: Smoke, Steam and Spindles
description: How a few engines, looms and rails in Britain changed how the world worked, and with it cities, classes, empires and ideas about progress.

checkpoints.name: The first engines
checkpoints.note: Newcomen's atmospheric engine pumps mines, Arkwright and the spinning jenny speed up cotton spinning, and James Watt improves the steam engine with the support of thinkers in the Lunar Society.

checkpoints.name: Iron and wealth
checkpoints.note: The Iron Bridge shows what cast iron can do, Adam Smith's Wealth of Nations explains the new economy, and Stephenson's Rocket proves steam trains can work.

checkpoints.name: The railway age
checkpoints.note: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens, telegraph wires follow the lines, and Brunel builds tunnels and ships. Railway Mania ruins investors, Dickens writes of the poor, and Marx publishes The Communist Manifesto.

checkpoints.name: Workshop of the world
checkpoints.note: The Great Exhibition shows British industry to the world. The Bessemer process makes cheap steel, cables and the Suez Canal shrink distances, and the telephone arrives.

checkpoints.name: The second wave
checkpoints.note: Steam turbines, electricity and steel take over from the first generation, and the industrial revolution spreads to Germany, the United States and Japan.
